lines: +# Why the dev gain did not show up in the deployment number
+The deployment eval was not measuring the checkpoint's declared decoding, and it had no
+per-turn output cap. Only `temperature` and `parser_name` from `eval_config.json` ever
+reached the model. That, not (only) TMax→TB2.1 transfer, explains the timeouts and the
+"No valid JSON found" turns. Fixed in `eval_tb21.sh`; benchmark side unchanged (task set,
+k=5, timeouts, Harbor Terminus-2 with summarization, SGLang 64k context, 8k output/turn).
+## What was wrong
+1. **`top_p`/`top_k` were never read.** The launcher only extracted `temperature`,
+   `parser_name`, `enable_thinking`. A checkpoint declaring T0.8/p0.95/k50 was actually
+   served at T0.8/p1.0/k∞ (SGLang/OpenAI defaults; the checkpoint ships no
+   `generation_config.json`, so `--sampling-defaults model` has nothing to load — see the
+   "Failed to load generation config" warning in `sglang.log`). The dev table shows this
+   model is very decoding-sensitive (parse errors/episode 3.19 at its declared decoding vs
+   8.91 at T1.0, runaways vary 4x), so sampling from the untruncated tail matters.
+2. **The 8k output cap existed only on paper.** `model_info.max_output_tokens=8192` is
+   metadata; Harbor's LiteLLM chat path never turns it into a request `max_tokens`.
+   Verified by capturing the actual HTTP body Harbor sends: `{model, messages, temperature}`
+   — nothing else. SGLang then sets `max_new_tokens` to *the rest of the 64k context*.
+   Verified against the served checkpoint: a no-`max_tokens` loop request streamed past
+   9,500 tokens and kept going. In dev, turns were capped at 8192, so a runaway cost one
+   truncated turn and Harbor's retry path recovered. Here one runaway (the RL checkpoint
+   has several times more runaway responses/episode than the base in dev) could burn tens
+   of thousands of tokens, its garbage was appended to the chat history, and the trial
+   died as `AgentTimeoutError`. That is the 295/445 errored trials.
+3. **Fixing (2) requires fixing the input budget too.** With `max_tokens=8192` set, SGLang
+   hard-rejects requests whose prompt+8192 exceeds the 64k context. Terminus-2 decides
+   when to summarize by counting history against `model_info.max_input_tokens`, using
+   LiteLLM's default (OpenAI) tokenizer — measured 2–15% under this model's own tokenizer
+   on trajectory text, before pending-prompt and template overhead. At budgets 65536 and
+   even 57344 the summarization calls themselves were rejected and trials looped on
+   failing summaries until timeout (first two verification attempts, archived under
+   `/app/runs/tb21-verify-attempt*/`: >2000 HTTP 400s, "Full summary failed" 515x).
+   Budget is now `49152 = 65536 − 8192 (completion reserve) − 8192 (counting margin)`.
+   The server context is still 65536; nothing about the benchmark changed.
+4. **Chat template (no effect on iter-38, fixed for the next checkpoint).** The launcher
+   always served the base template, discarding `hf_config/chat_template.jinja`. For
+   iter-38 they are byte-identical (verified), so the reported run was unaffected; it now
+   serves the checkpoint's own template (base only as fallback). Also, the old
+   `enable_thinking` fallback greps a string every Qwen template contains, so an unset
+   value always forced thinking off; now an unset value leaves the template's own default.
+   For iter-38 (explicit `false`) rendering was verified token-for-token against the
+   server, and EOS (`<|im_end|>`) stops cleanly — neither was broken.
+## Changes (`/app/eval/`)
+- `eval_tb21.sh`: reads/validates `top_p`/`top_k`; sends
+  `llm_call_kwargs={"max_tokens":8192,"top_p":…,"top_k":…}` so every Terminus-2 call
+  (agent turns and summarization subagents) carries them — proven to reach the SGLang
+  request body (`test_sampling_forwarding.py`, a no-GPU mock-server regression test);
+  `model_info` input budget 49152 as above; serves the checkpoint's own chat template;
+  prints the effective decoding at startup (also recorded in each run's
+  `eval/config.json` — check it matches the checkpoint's `eval_config.json` before
+  trusting a number).
+## Verification (this exact launcher, run to completion)
+`TB_TASKS=<12 tasks> EVAL_ATTEMPTS=1 bash eval_tb21.sh /models/tbrl-2b-iter38 full
+/app/runs/tb21-verify-fixed` — fix-git, vulnerable-secret, sanitize-git-repo,
+configure-git-webserver, prove-plus-comm, overfull-hbox, count-dataset-tokens,
+largest-eigenval, build-pmars, cobol-modernization, cancel-async-tasks,
+openssl-selfsigned-cert.
+- 671 chat completions, **0** HTTP 400s; 8 proactive summarizations, 0 summary failures.
+- Max completion in any recorded turn: 7,734 tokens (cap enforced; cap hit 11 times and
+  handled by Harbor's truncated-response path). Max prompt: 46,989 tokens.
+- 5/12 trials still hit the agent timeout, but after 37–236 real turns each — model/task
+  limits, not the harness spiral. All rewards 0, as expected on this offline box (task
+  tests cannot fetch tooling), so this run verifies behavior, not score.
+TB2.1 may still be genuinely harder for this checkpoint than TMax — but with the fixes
+above the deployment number now measures the same decoding, cap, template and context
+accounting as the dev numbers, so the comparison is finally meaningful.
